paper.title: Language Generation in the Limit: Noise, Loss, and Feedback
paper.summary: Studies exact, noisy, lossy, no-sample, repetition-allowing, and feedback variants of language generation, proves sharp separations between adjacent finite omission and noise levels and between known and unknown finite noise, characterizes no-sample generation, and gives a feedback-identification theorem. The registry distinguishes native P12 result wrappers from reused P10, P06, Gold, and P02 infrastructure and records repaired source proofs and the remaining total-query interface gap.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom seventeen-card surface has fifteen fully covered cards and two partially covered infinite-feedback cards. Fifty-seven unique P12-native canonical declarations cover the summary theorems, principal semantic definitions, constructions, and detailed results. The only source-result interface gap is the every-round query syntax in Definition 6.1 and Algorithm 4: Lean proves the cover theorems with an optional-query controller but does not expose the routine dummy-query totalization adapter.
specializations: Summary Theorems 1.1 and 1.7 are P12-native wrappers, but their fixed counterexample is the concurrent P10 Theorem 4.3 witness transported from the signed integers to the naturals; P10 declarations are not counted as P12 canonical endpoints.

The reverse noisy-to-no-sample reductions are stated over the paper's canonical universe of natural numbers; the forward reductions and most structural statements are polymorphic over countable universes.

Theorem 1.8 is exposed first for an explicitly indexed language family. A separate native wrapper obtains such an indexing for a nonempty countable extensional class, while the canonical claim endpoint remains the source-shaped indexed-family result.

All linked constructions are deterministic mathematical functions, often selected classically. The registry makes no machine-level computability, oracle implementation, query-complexity, or runtime inference.

The noisy-examples, closure-dimension, nonuniform-cover, and complete-informant developments are proof infrastructure or bridge provenance only; their declarations are not counted again as P12 coverage.
gaps: Definition 6.1 and Algorithm 4 issue a membership query on every paper round, whereas the shared Lean feedback interface permits wait rounds with no query. The semantic cover-to-feedback core is proved, but no P12 theorem totalizes every none action to an ignored dummy query.

No P12 claim has human correspondence coverage. Source assessment and claim grouping are AI audit work, while kernel checking establishes only Lean declaration existence, types, modules, and allowed axioms.

The semantic algorithms do not establish effective representations of arbitrary language classes, decidable membership in class-derived cores, machine execution, or runtime bounds; those are outside the paper's stated theorem claims and this custom inventory.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Seventeen claim groups: summary Theorems 1.1--1.8; Definitions 2.8--2.13; the Definitions 4.1--4.3, Algorithms 1--2, and Theorems 4.4--4.5 equivalence cluster; Theorem 4.6, Algorithm 3, and Theorem 4.7; Definitions 4.8--4.10 and Theorems 4.11--4.12; Definitions 4.13--4.14, Lemmas 4.16--4.17, and Theorem 4.15; Definitions 5.1--5.6, Lemma 5.4, and Theorem 5.7; Definitions 6.1--6.2, Algorithm 4, Theorem 6.3, and Corollary 6.4; Definitions 6.5--6.6, Algorithm 5, and Theorem 6.7; Definitions 6.8--6.9 and Algorithm 6 grouped with Theorem 1.8; and Appendix Definitions A.1--A.3, Algorithm 7, and Lemmas A.4--A.6.
exclusions: Definitions 2.1--2.7 restate inherited exact-generation, consistency, closure, and closure-dimension interfaces; they remain claim assumptions rather than duplicate standalone cards.

The repeated Section 3 statement of Theorem 1.1 is represented by the single summary-result card, and proof equations, witness-class definitions, phase states, cursor invariants, continuation lemmas, and other proof-only helpers are not separate source claims.
The additional i=0 sentence after Theorem 5.7 is a direct instance of the registered hierarchy theorem and receives no duplicate card.
Concurrent-work attribution, related work, roadmap, figure prose, closing remarks, and bibliographic statements are outside this minimal result-centered scope.
P10 witness declarations, the P06 noisy-examples bridge, P02 closure and cover infrastructure, and Gold complete-informant results are provenance rather than P12 claim coverage.
Machine computability, representations of arbitrary semantic classes, runtime, and asymptotic query complexity are not inferred from the source's mathematical algorithm pseudocode.

claims.title: A nonuniform and a uniform no-sample class can have a nongeneratable union
claims.statement_summary: There exist two classes of infinite languages, one generatable in the limit without samples and the other uniformly generatable without samples, whose union is not generatable in the ordinary repetition-free model.

source_assessment.notes: The source gives an independent signed-integer diagonal construction. The concurrent P10 provenance concerns Lean proof reuse, not the truth or attribution of the P12 statement.

formalization.notes: The P12-native theorem preserves both no-sample positive guarantees and the union lower bound after transporting the concurrent fixed witness from the signed integers to the naturals.

lean_links.notes: This is a native P12 source-result wrapper. Its proof reuses P10's Theorem 4.3 witness and does not count the P10 declaration as P12 coverage.

relations.notes: Lean transports and repackages the concurrent P10 fixed witness, while the P12 paper supplies its own proof.

claims.title: Uniform and nonuniform noisy generation coincide with the corresponding no-sample models
claims.statement_summary: For classes of infinite languages, uniform noisy generation is equivalent to uniform generation without samples, and nonuniform noisy generation is equivalent to generation in the limit without samples.

source_assessment.notes: The result is retained, but the reverse reductions in the detailed proof probe on the finite prefix 0,...,t as though it were already a noisy enumeration of an arbitrary target. Lean supplies the missing ordered-prefix continuation argument.

formalization.notes: The native summary endpoint combines the two repaired detailed equivalences with the source quantifier order.

lean_links.notes: The UUS hypothesis makes the paper's standing infinite-language convention explicit.

relations.notes: Summary Theorem 1.2 packages detailed Theorems 4.4 and 4.5.

claims.title: No-sample generation in the limit is characterized by an increasing infinite-core cover
claims.statement_summary: A class is generatable in the limit without samples exactly when it is the union of a nondecreasing sequence of subclasses, each having infinite common intersection.

source_assessment.notes: The source biconditional and its cover quantifiers are coherent.

formalization.notes: Lean preserves the complete nondecreasing-cover, union, and infinite-intersection quantifier structure in both directions.

lean_links.notes: No computable enumeration of the cover or common cores is inferred.

relations.notes: The countable-class Theorem 4.7 is a simplified specialization of this general cover theorem.

claims.title: Any uniform or nonuniform generator tolerates arbitrary infinite omissions
claims.statement_summary: A generator that succeeds uniformly, or with a target-dependent threshold, on every exact repetition-free enumeration continues to succeed with the same threshold when the adversary presents any infinite repetition-free subset of the target.

source_assessment.notes: The printed proof omits the finite-prefix obligation needed to extend each lossy prefix to an exact enumeration of the target. That extension exists, and the Lean proof supplies it explicitly; the theorem statement is retained with this proof-repair qualification.

formalization.notes: The native wrapper states both same-generator preservation directions.

lean_links.notes: The source's standing infinite-language convention is explicit as UUS.

relations.notes: Summary Theorem 1.4 packages detailed Theorems 4.11 and 4.12.

claims.title: Every adjacent finite omission and known-noise level is strictly separated
claims.statement_summary: For each i, one class is generatable in the limit with at most i omissions and with known noise level i, but is not generatable with i+1 omissions and is not generatable with known noise level i+1.

source_assessment.notes: The summary's "or/either" wording can be misread as a disjunction. The detailed theorems, and the Lean endpoint, establish the intended stronger reading: one marker-and-tail class simultaneously satisfies all four positive and negative omission/noise properties.

formalization.notes: The summary endpoint packages all four positive and negative components for the literal shared witness.

lean_links.notes: The UUS field records the paper's standing infinite-language convention.

claims.title: Knowing each finite noise bound is strictly stronger than tolerating an unknown finite bound
claims.statement_summary: There exists one class for which, for every finite i, some generator succeeds when the noise level i is supplied in advance, yet no single generator succeeds against all finite noisy enumerations when the bound is hidden.

source_assessment.notes: The intended separation has the stated existential order, but the printed argument contains an element-versus-subset (∈/⊆) typo and phase/time-index defects in the diagonal construction. Lean formalizes the repaired intended argument.

formalization.notes: Lean contains the complete positive family and the direct infinite diagonal lower bound for the literal source witness.

lean_links.notes: The source's exact existential order is retained; the stronger UUS facade is intentionally not canonical.

claims.title: Infinite membership feedback is strictly stronger, while every finite budget equals no feedback
claims.statement_summary: Some language class is generatable with unrestricted membership feedback but not without feedback and not with any fixed finite query budget; for every class and fixed finite budget, feedback generation has exactly the power of ordinary repetition-free generation.

source_assessment.notes: The claim is retained. The detailed proof of Theorem 6.7 uses an inconsistent left/right convention for its decision tree; Lean replaces that step with eventual agreement of the finite real query transcript.

formalization.notes: The P12 wrapper proves the strict semantic witness in an optional-query feedback interface, and Lean fully proves finite-feedback equivalence. It does not expose the syntactic adapter making a membership query on every source round.

claims.statement_summary: For any explicitly indexed countable family of languages over the naturals, Algorithm 6 queries the current universe element, maintains the indices consistent with positive data and membership answers, and eventually outputs an index naming the target uniformly over its exact positive enumerations.

formalization.notes: The native endpoint formalizes the source family interface and Algorithm 6. The proof reuses Gold complete-informant elimination internally but counts only P12 declarations.

claims.title: Finite-noise enumerations and projection define the paper's noisy semantic interface
claims.statement_summary: A noisy enumeration is injective, covers every target point, and has only finitely many extraneous values; uniform, nonuniform, and limit noisy success differ only in the stabilization quantifiers. Projection intersects each language with a smaller universe and discards finite projected languages.

source_assessment.notes: The definitions consistently use the paper's no-repetition convention and discard finite projections because languages are infinite by convention.

formalization.notes: Six direct P12 definitions expose the noisy stream, three stabilization quantifiers, and both projection operations.

claims.title: Algorithms 1 and 2 realize the detailed noisy and no-sample equivalences
claims.statement_summary: A no-sample generator can skip outputs already observed in a noisy stream, while a noisy generator can be probed and thinned to an injective autonomous output stream; these reductions establish the uniform and nonuniform biconditionals of Theorems 4.4 and 4.5.

source_assessment.notes: The retained reverse implications need a semantic repair: the finite probe 0,...,t is not itself a noisy enumeration of an arbitrary target. Lean proves that every ordered injective probe prefix extends to a full noisy enumeration before extracting fresh record outputs.

claims.title: Countable covers by uniformly or nonuniformly generatable classes admit feedback generation

claims.title: First-occurrence filtering makes repetitions immaterial in all three generation models
claims.statement_summary: Definitions A.1--A.3 measure success on repetition-allowing presentations. Algorithm 7 causally removes repeated observations, and Lemmas A.4--A.6 show that uniform, nonuniform, and generation-in-the-limit power is unchanged for classes of infinite languages.

source_assessment.notes: The claims are retained. The printed A.4--A.5 proofs confuse raw zero-based time with a uniform distinct-cardinality threshold, and the A.6 proof starts from the wrong generator type and uses an undefined d*. formalization.notes: All three source definitions, the causal adapter, and all three repaired biconditionals are maintained. The infinite-language hypothesis is explicit because finite targets admit repeated but not injective infinite presentations.
